title: The Blaschka Object Network — Dublin Shipping Failure and Replacement Register
scope: A workshop-side 1887 Dublin cluster in which dealer routing, shipper documentation, accidental landing at Bristol, delay, breakage and replacement can be followed across institutional orders. The cluster links W. J. Sollas at Trinity College Dublin and A. C. Haddon at the Royal College of Science, Dublin, through Robert Damon and a Hamburg forwarding route.
methodological_guard: The OCR date and the Haddon case-prefix/forwarder spelling are imperfect. The transaction sequence is retained without silently repairing those fields. The Bristol landing is described by the workshop as resulting from a mistake in the shipper's note; no carrier is assigned until another document names it.

events.response: Fresh examples of the two damaged models were placed into the subsequent Haddon consignment.
events.research_value: A documentary error altered the physical route, produced delay and probable breakage, and was corrected by embedding replacements in a different customer's shipment. Logistics feedback therefore crossed order boundaries.

parallel_haddon_archive.repository: University of St Andrews Special Collections
parallel_haddon_archive.content: Nine Haddon letters to D'Arcy Wentworth Thompson about marine natural history, specimen supply and exchange between museums and collecting work in Ireland.
parallel_haddon_archive.status: same-period Haddon network context, not Blaschka evidence
parallel_haddon_archive.research_value: Useful for reconstructing Haddon's ordinary exchange and museum-supply practices around the time of the Blaschka order.

research_observation: The Dublin cluster gives a unusually concrete failure chain: shipper's note → wrong port → delay → breakage → replacement → consolidation into another customer's insured case. It therefore provides direct evidence that paperwork errors and physical damage were coupled, and that the workshop managed failure through subsequent network traffic rather than treating each order as a closed transaction.
